clesRetenues: Q Tito Labarta (Goldman Sachs) - impact of Desenrola on risk-adjusted NIM, 2027 growth outlook: a minority of the improvement tied to Desenrola, the majority to seasonality/solid performance; no structural deterioration observed.

Q Jorge Kuri (Morgan Stanley) - KPIs supporting the sustainability of the 12,4% risk-adjusted NIM, AI contribution to credit: AI models more powerful than logistic regression, risk framework unchanged, under-levered balance sheet with an opportunity to reallocate deposits.

Q Eduardo Rosman (BTG Pactual) - appointment of David Vélez to the OpenAI board: AI judged the most significant technological transformation, the role offering privileged access to frontier AI development.

Q Pedro Leduc (Itaú BBA) - accounting treatment of Desenrola, pace of unsecured lending, private payroll: Desenrola portfolio in stage 3, minimal ECL impact (<10M$); unsecured loan growth normalising.

Q Yuri Fernandes (JP Morgan) - net income growth trajectory post-1Md$, Chroma targets: Brazil remains the largest opportunity despite the size of the base, ARPAC 17$ vs 40-45$ for the incumbent banks.
Q Geoffrey Elliott (Autonomous) - headcount decline (10 500 to 10 400), AI productivity impact: decline tied to return-to-office attrition, rehires offsetting the majority of the losses.
Q Daniel Vaz (Safra) - AI priorities in card funding/deposit optimisation, pricing strategy: priority on NPS and product quality alongside cost optimisation, pricing personalised by customer.

Q Craig Muir (FT Partners) - transferability of the US model, timeline for rebuilding the credit model: nuFormer platform and credit expertise transposable quickly, 12-30 months for the US-specific data richness.

Q Mario Pierry (Bank of America) - risk-adjusted NIM beat vs Q1 guidance (expected 10,5-10,8%, delivered 12,4%), NPL reconciliation: ~1/3 of the outperformance tied to Desenrola, ~2/3 to credit performance and to the ramp from Q1 into Q2.

Q Jorge Kuri (Morgan Stanley) - SME product launch in Brazil: a base of 5M SME customers built at zero acquisition cost through cross-sell, new credit lines leveraging government guarantees, an opportunity described as a "blue ocean".

Q Yuri Fernandes (JPMorgan) - read on asset quality and conservatism of provisioning: provisions not reflecting a directional macro forecast, a conservative approach assuming a future worse than the past.

Q Eduardo Rosman (BTG Pactual) - differences in sentiment between local and foreign investors: three polarising topics identified (asset quality, international expansion, AI); long-standing local scepticism on new markets.

Q Daniel Vaz (Safra) - Brazil unsecured vs secured strategy, private payroll approach: an early-stage opportunity (7% of the profit pool), private payroll deliberately slower (perceived underestimated default risk).

Q Marcelo Mizrahi (Bradesco BBI) - efficiency ratio forecast, private payroll impact: ~2/3 of the Q1 outperformance tied to timing (marketing, real estate pushed back), ~1/3 structural (AI gains, hiring discipline).

Q Tito Labarta (Goldman Sachs) - high-income segment performance, secured lending opportunity outside FGTS: new premium card products boosting engagement, high-income base +24% YoY, "super core" segment with 3 Brazilians out of 5 already customers.

pointsCles: Net income crossed $1B for the first time at $1.1B (+49% YoY, +17% QoQ) with a record 33% ROE; risk-adjusted NIM jumped to a record 12.4% from 9.5%, with ~1/3 of the margin surprise from the Desenrola debt-renegotiation program and ~2/3 from underlying credit performance and yield ramp on Q1 loan growth.

Asset quality debate dominated Q&A: 90+ NPL up 35bp to 6.9% (seasonal migration plus portfolio mix shift, per management), 15-90d NPL improved 16bp to 4.8%, coverage at 244% and provisioning at 113% of new 15+ formation; first call for new CFO Rob Livingston, who succeeded Guilherme Lago.

AI platform NuFormer moved to a hybrid linear-attention architecture (4x context length, training and inference speed; same predictive power with 20M vs 400M fine-tuning rows), now powering core credit models, >60% of Brazil customer support and 100+ campaigns; David Velez joined OpenAI's board.

hypothese.summary: Leading neobank in Latin America; Q2 26 confirms and reinforces the thesis (record net income >1,1 Md$, ROE 33%, record risk-adjusted NIM 12,4%) - Omnium adjusted EPS for 2026 raised from 0,88$ to 0,91$ (+3,7%) to reflect the H1 beat, remaining above the current sell-side consensus (~0,85$) on the assumption of continued momentum rather than a flattening in H2.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Leading LatAm neobank (Brazil, Mexico, Colombia) in profitable hypergrowth: Q2 26 net income above 1.1bn for the first time, record 33% ROE. The three-pillar thesis strengthens: Brazil already highly profitable (activity rate through 86% for the first time), Mexico accelerating post-breakeven (banking license obtained early July; ARPAC already 12.3 vs 5.6 for Brazil at a comparable stage), and the US expansion as a near-free option. The whole 2026-2030 trajectory was lifted +3.7% on the H1 realization (ancrage beat_h1_2026).

== THESIS READ ==
- Mexico is the compounding surprise: ARPAC at 2x Brazil's comparable-stage level says the second market may be RICHER, not just bigger. Watch: Mexico deposit growth and credit-book seasoning under the new license.
- Brazil's activity rate >86% shows the mature market still deepens - cross-sell (secured lending, payroll loans, investments) is the engine. Watch: risk-adjusted NIM holding ~12.4% as mix shifts to secured.
- The +3.7% uplift is realization-based, not guidance-based (Nu guides nothing) - documented distinctly from the scorecard function. Watch: H2 confirming the run-rate.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Fintech base convention: 'ebit' IS pretax income (funding cost in the top line) - finNet=0 by construction in the bridge; the only wedge is tax. Managerial 32% normative vs IFRS effective ~26% in FY25 (+239M documented residual, not reconducted). No buyback program; dilution minimal.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 24.4bn (+50%), pretax 6.56bn, net 4.46bn / EPS 0.91; 2027-2030: revenue +30%/yr fading, pretax margin 27% -> 33.5%, tax 32% managerial. Watch: Brazil credit cycle (unemployment/delinquency); Mexico funding cost trajectory; US entry economics; FX translation (results in USD, business in BRL/MXN).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 (Nov); Mexico license-enabled product launches; US move; Brazil payroll-loan share gains.

ancrages.moteur: Cumulative net income H1 26 of 1,971 Md$ (871 M$ Q1 + 1,1 Md$ Q2, a record), record ROE 33% and record risk-adjusted NIM 12,4% in Q2 - uniform +3,7% raise to the omniumCA/omniumEBIT/omniumNet/omniumEPS 2026-2030 trajectory vs the previous refresh
Managerial tax rate maintained at ~32% (management guidance IFRS 15-20% + managerial 30-35% communicated in Q1 26, not revised in Q2 26, consistent with regional peers)

Consolidated efficiency ratio targeted at ~20% on an annual average basis, reaffirmed in Q2 26 despite a Q1 (17,6%) and a Q2 (19,5%) below that target - EBIT margin trajectory anchored on that discipline rather than on extrapolating the most favourable quarters
US expansion impact explicitly capped by management at <100 bps on the 2026-2027 consolidated efficiency ratio, a "call option" approach with a small capital outlay

No significant buyback programme nor any new material dilution identified this quarter - diluted share trajectory carried over unchanged from the previous refresh (~4,9 Md shares in 2026, a slight gradual decline over 2027-2030 tied to the historical dynamics of the share plans)
